env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection. Disclose unknown reply timing and do not infer reply links from speaker order alone.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Computation and source suitability:
  - Use code for raw counts, regex/literal matching, supplied numeric columns and fixed
    computational recipes. Use a prompt when the measurement requires understanding meaning.
    Do not add semantic filtering to a raw count or URL detector merely because outcome text
    may occur in its source. Disclose that contamination risk; raw text is not outcome-free.
  - Semantic feature specs must exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome
    resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence of the construct. Generic
    platform/delta-rule discussion remains eligible. Explicitly requested semantic exclusions
    remain part of any measurement; never remove one just to force code.
  - Use current supplied text unless the hypothesis restricts time. Deleting edits does not
    recover initial/pre-outcome text. No supplied comment/edit timestamps establish timing.
    If a required temporal measurement is unavailable, explain it and set term=null.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring a different outcome or an
    outcome-revealing predictor is unsupported: preserve the claim, explain it and set
    term=null rather than substituting another test or a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument body, in the OP's own assertions, makes an explicit comparison to an established scientific or historical norm/standard/precedent; else 0.
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP text). Return 1 if the OP's own text explicitly compares their claim, case or subject to an established scientific norm (e.g., accepted scientific consensus, standard scientific practice/findings) or an established historical norm/precedent (e.g., how past societies or historical standards handled something), with the comparison stated explicitly (e.g., 'like', 'unlike', 'compared to', 'as in'). Return 0 if there is no such comparison. Attributed quotations count only if the OP adopts them as their own comparison. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Empty argument gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Do not use title or any other column.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with and without argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms have the same association with delta (view change).
decomposed.h1: Discussions where argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms is 1 are associated with lower view change (delta) than those where it is 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'established norms' judged by the annotator from the current argument text; no external verification. Current text may contain edits or outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence, but deleted initial text cannot be recovered. Association only, not causal. Binary OLS is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: expresses_fear_social_rejection
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument text explicitly expresses fear of social rejection, ostracism, or isolation (OP's own assertion, not a quotation); else 0.
features.spec: Read only the OP `argument` text. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear, worry or dread of being rejected, shunned, excluded, judged into isolation, or left alone/isolated by others socially because of the view or related behavior. Return 0 otherwise. Do not count quoted or attributed text from others unless the OP adopts it as their own fear; quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome and post-outcome resolution updates as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is not evidence of fear. Empty or missing argument gives null. Output 0 or 1.

features.name: states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument states beliefs/reasoning without any emotional self-defense (no defensive emotional self-protection, e.g. fear, hurt, defensiveness about being judged); else 0.
features.spec: Read only the OP `argument` text. Return 1 if the OP states their beliefs and reasons and contains no emotional self-defense, i.e. no passages where the OP defends or protects themselves emotionally (e.g. pre-emptive defensiveness about being judged, expressed hurt, fear of rejection, pleas for sympathy or protection from attack). Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense is present in the OP's own voice. Quotations from others do not count unless adopted by the OP. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome. Empty or missing argument gives null. Output 0 or 1.

decomposed.h0: Rows with `expresses_fear_social_rejection` = 1 have the same view-change rate as other rows, holding `states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense` fixed.
decomposed.h1: Rows with `expresses_fear_social_rejection` = 1 have a lower view-change rate than rows with `states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense` = 1.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured. The OLS coefficient on the fear feature is relative to the omitted neither group (neither fear nor a plain-belief label), not directly the fear-vs-plain contrast; the exact difference of the two coefficients cannot be expressed as a single term. Fear and plain-belief features should rarely overlap (fear implies emotional self-defense). Uses current OP argument text only; it may contain edits or outcome announcements (excluded by the prompts but not guaranteed absent), and original unedited text is not recoverable. Linear probability association only, not causal. Fear of rejection is judged from text, not a measured trait.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: precedent_comment_count
features.definition: Count of counter-argument comments (by other users) that cite at least one specific, real, functioning institutional precedent (e.g., a named law, policy, court, organization or country's working system) as support against the OP's view.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to understand what each comment is rebutting. Return the integer count of comments that, in the commenter's own assertions, cite a specific named or clearly identifiable institutional precedent that is operating/has operated in practice (existing law, policy, court ruling, organization, or jurisdiction's functioning system) as evidence against the OP's view. A source quoted merely as a rebuttal target, or an abstract hypothetical institution, does not count. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. A comment may count here and also in `normative_principle_comment_count` only if it clearly does both. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

features.name: normative_principle_comment_count
features.definition: Count of counter-argument comments (by other users) whose argument relies on abstract normative principles (e.g., fairness, rights, morality, justice) without citing a specific functioning institutional precedent.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to interpret each comment's target. Return the integer count of comments whose main counter-argument rests on abstract normative or moral principles (e.g., fairness, rights, justice, autonomy, what ought to be) and which cite no specific, identifiable functioning institutional precedent. Comments relying on precedents, purely empirical or personal-anecdote arguments, or off-topic remarks do not count. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: Holding `normative_principle_comment_count` fixed, `precedent_comment_count` has no association with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Holding `normative_principle_comment_count` fixed, higher `precedent_comment_count` is associated with a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Comparison is operationalised as per-row counts of comments in each named group, fitted by OLS (linear probability). The coefficient on precedent count is not a direct contrast beta_precedent - beta_normative; the contrast is not expressed by this term. Counts depend on number of available comments; comments are unordered, with no per-comment outcomes, so this is a row-level association only, not causal. Current text may include outcome announcements or later replies; prompts exclude them but contamination risk remains. 'Functioning' is judged from the comment's wording only; no external verification.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: The supplied precomputed log_length value for the discussion row, used as is.
features.spec: df['supplied_log_length'] = pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce'); missing or non-numeric gives null. No recomputation or log-base assumption.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: log_length is used exactly as supplied. Its construction, source text (title, argument, comments or conversation), log base and timing are undocumented. It is not equated with word count. It may include text written after the OP changed their view, so it may be contaminated by the outcome. The test is an association, not a causal effect. The OLS is a linear probability model on binary delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument text contains at least one explicit admission of uncertainty about their own view or claims (e.g., 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure'); else 0.
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly admits uncertainty, fallibility or doubt about their own view or claims (e.g. 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'I may be mistaken'). Return 0 otherwise. Do not count generic hedges not signalling the OP's own uncertainty, uncertainty in quoted text from others unless the OP adopts it, or any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, edit reporting the outcome, or post-outcome resolution update. Empty argument gives 0; missing/malformed gives null.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument text explicitly asserts absolute certainty or incontrovertibility of their view (e.g., 'undeniably', 'no possible doubt'); else 0.
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty, or that their view is beyond doubt or cannot be wrong (e.g. 'I am 100% certain', 'undeniable', 'there is no doubt'). Return 0 otherwise. Do not count quoted others' certainty unless OP adopts it, ordinary strong opinion without explicit certainty claims, or any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, edit reporting the outcome, or post-outcome resolution update. Empty argument gives 0; missing/malformed gives null.

decomposed.h0: Holding `op_asserts_absolute_certainty` fixed, `op_admits_uncertainty` has no association with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Holding `op_asserts_absolute_certainty` fixed, `op_admits_uncertainty` is associated with a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Association only. The comparison is operationalized as two separate binary indicators (the groups may overlap or both be 0); the coefficient on op_admits_uncertainty is not a direct contrast with the absolute-certainty group, which the contract cannot express as a single difference. Current argument text may contain edits or outcome announcements, which are excluded from the semantic measurement but timing of edits is unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged
features.definition: Count of distinct factual premises asserted in the OP's argument that are challenged (disputed as factually wrong, unsupported or contradicted by evidence) by at least one counter-comment in OC_comments.
features.spec: Read title and argument (to identify the OP's factual premises) and parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return a non-negative integer: the number of distinct empirical/factual premises stated in the OP's argument that are challenged by at least one comment, counting each premise once even if several comments challenge it. Challenge = the comment disputes the truth, accuracy or evidential basis of the premise as a matter of fact. Do not count challenges to values, logic/inference only, definitions, or preferences, and do not count agreement or mere clarification questions. Attribute challenges only to the commenter's own assertions, not to material they quote from the OP or others unless adopted. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty comment list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments or missing argument gives null.

features.name: share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises
features.definition: Share of counter-comments in OC_comments that each challenge two or more distinct factual premises of the OP's argument.
features.spec: Read title and argument (to identify the OP's factual premises) and parse OC_comments. For each comment, decide whether that single comment itself challenges (disputes the truth, accuracy or evidential basis of) at least two distinct factual premises stated in the OP's argument; challenges spread across separate comments do not combine. Return the number of such comments divided by the total number of comments, a value in [0,1]. Do not count challenges to only values, logic, definitions or preferences. Count only the commenter's own assertions, not quoted material unless adopted. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed OC_comments or argument gives null.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between distinct_factual_premises_challenged and view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher distinct_factual_premises_challenged is associated with a higher probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: "Frequently" is operationalized by the share of comments each challenging at least two distinct factual premises. The term tests that share, adjusting for the row-level count of distinct premises challenged. The count feature is the second named measurement, but its coefficient is not the tested term. OC_comments is an unordered list with no per-comment timestamps, so conclusions are about association only. Current text may contain outcome announcements, and the prompts exclude them. The factual versus non-factual distinction requires judgment. The two features are likely correlated, and OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: counter_argument_comment_count
features.definition: Number of entries in the parsed OC_comments list of counter-argument comments by other users.
features.spec: import json; df['counter_argument_comment_count'] = df['OC_comments'].apply(lambda s: len(json.loads(s)) if isinstance(s,str) else None); malformed JSON or non-list -> null; valid empty list -> 0.

decomposed.h0: counter_argument_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher counter_argument_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (fewer comments, lower likelihood).
decomposed.note: Operationalized as the count of available OC_comments entries (counts comments, not distinct commenters). The list is the supplied available counter-comments and may not be the full discussion; it may be selected in relation to the outcome (e.g., delta-awarding comments included), a contamination/selection risk. Timing unknown. Linear OLS on a binary outcome (linear probability model); association only. 'Original argument contains' is read as responses to the original post.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: Count of distinct counter-arguments (separate reasons/points opposing the OP's view) across the other users' comments in OC_comments.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's view is. Return a non-negative integer: the number of distinct counter-arguments, i.e. substantively different points challenging the OP's view, counted across all comments; repeated or paraphrased points count once, and several distinct points in one comment each count. Do not count agreement, questions, jokes, clarifications without challenge, or off-topic text. Exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome; generic delta-rule discussion is not a counter-argument. Quoted OP text is not a counter-argument unless the commenter refutes it. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

features.name: has_three_plus_counterarguments
features.definition: 1 if distinct_counterargument_count is at least 3, else 0.
features.spec: df['has_three_plus_counterarguments'] = (df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3).astype(int), with null where `distinct_counterargument_count` is null.

decomposed.h0: has_three_plus_counterarguments has no association with whether the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_plus_counterarguments = 1 are associated with a higher likelihood of delta=1 than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Counts only comments available in OC_comments (the posted comments); distinct is judged semantically with no supplied ranking or chronology. Comments may be a subset and may contain outcome announcements; the prompt excludes those. Association only, not causal. The binary feature's source_columns list the original columns read via the referenced feature.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_has_absolute_certainty_marker
features.definition: 1 if the OP's post title contains an absolute certainty marker (e.g., always, never, all, none, obviously, undeniably, definitely, certainly, without a doubt, 100%), else 0.
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title itself uses wording that expresses absolute certainty or exceptionless universality about the OP's claim (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'everyone', 'no one', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'definitely', 'without a doubt', 'objectively', '100%', 'impossible'). Return 0 if the title has no such marker (hedged or merely stated claims, including 'CMV:' prefix alone, are 0). Judge by meaning in context: a word like 'all' counts only when used as an absolute quantifier/certainty marker of the claim, not incidentally. Ignore any view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports if present. Return null if the title is missing or malformed. Output 0 or 1.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose titles contain absolute certainty markers (title_has_absolute_certainty_marker=1) have the same likelihood of OP view change as those without.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_has_absolute_certainty_marker=1 have a lower likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: absolute certainty markers are judged by an LLM from the current title with an illustrative, non-exhaustive lexicon. Association only, OLS linear probability model on delta. Title text could in principle contain edits/outcome text, though rarely; no timing information is available.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own title/argument explicitly invites critique or challenge to their view, or uses tentative/hedged language about their own claim; else 0.
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, (a) explicitly invites critique, counterarguments or being challenged (e.g. 'change my view', 'convince me otherwise', 'tell me where I'm wrong'), or (b) frames their own position tentatively/hedged (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems to me', 'I could be wrong'). Return 0 if neither is present. Ignore quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it. Ignore the generic CMV subreddit boilerplate unless the OP personally adds an invitation. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes or post-outcome resolution updates as evidence. Empty or missing text: null. Output 0/1 only.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarations
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own title/argument states their position in absolute, definitive, unhedged terms (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'obviously', 'undeniably'); else 0.
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, presents their central position as absolute or definitive, using categorical/unhedged declarations (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'everyone', 'no one', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'it is a fact that', 'there is no way'). Return 0 if no such absolute declarations of their own view are present. Ignore quoted material attributed to others unless the OP adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes or post-outcome updates as evidence. Empty or missing text: null. Output 0/1 only. The feature is independent of the tentative/invitation feature; a text can be 1 on both or neither.

decomposed.h0: Holding op_uses_absolute_declarations fixed, op_invites_critique_or_tentative is not associated with the delta (view-change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Holding op_uses_absolute_declarations fixed, op_invites_critique_or_tentative is associated with a higher view-change rate.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured separately, so overlap and neither-group cases are preserved. The exact contrast (tentative/inviting minus absolute) is not a single coefficient in this OLS; the term tests the tentative/invite coefficient adjusted for the absolute feature, and the absolute coefficient should be read alongside it. Measured on current OP text only; title/argument may contain edits or outcome announcements, which the prompts exclude as evidence, but timing relative to the outcome is unknown. Association only, not causal. The 'tentative language' and 'explicit invitation' were merged into one OR feature per the hypothesis wording. Based on column descriptions; no rows were inspected.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: share_comments_citing_specific_real_world_examples
features.definition: Share of OC_comments counter-argument comments (by other users) that explicitly cite at least one specific real-world example (named real event, person, place, organization, study or concrete case) in support of their own counter-argument.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own argument explicitly cites at least one specific, identifiable real-world example (a named or concretely identified actual event, person, country, organization, study, product, or documented case) as support. Generic claims, hypotheticals, vague 'some people' statements, and invented scenarios do not count. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it as support for their point; quotations of the OP or background/rebuttal quotes do not count. Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; they are not evidence of an example. Generic delta-rule discussion is not an example. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. If the list is valid but empty, output null; if missing or malformed, output null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_citing_specific_real_world_examples has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_citing_specific_real_world_examples is associated with higher likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'discussions featuring' counter-arguments with examples is measured as the share of available OC_comments that cite specific real-world examples (an any-comment indicator is an alternative). Comments' timing and ordering are unknown; the comment list may include text after the view change, and prompt excludes outcome announcements. Association only, not causal. The empty-list null follows the share convention.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Share of OC_comments counterargument comments whose own assertions present measured, logical reasoning (calm, step-by-step inference or evidence-based argument).
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own argument contains measured, logical reasoning: explicit premises/inferences, evidence or counterexamples, presented in a calm, non-hostile tone. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Quoted text from others counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. A comment may be both logical and aggressive; judge each independently. Output the number of comments meeting the criterion divided by the total number of comments (0 to 1). Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null.

features.name: share_comments_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Share of OC_comments counterargument comments whose own wording shows emotional aggression (hostility, insults, contempt, angry attacks on the OP).
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own wording shows emotional aggression: insults, hostility, sneering contempt, angry or personal attacks toward the OP or others. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Quoted text from others counts only if the commenter adopts it. Mere disagreement or blunt but civil criticism is not aggression. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Output the number of aggressive comments divided by the total number of comments (0 to 1). Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: Holding share_comments_emotional_aggression fixed, share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Holding share_comments_emotional_aggression fixed, higher share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning is positively associated with the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Both comparison groups are measured as separate shares of comments. The coefficient on the logical-reasoning share is tested, not the contrast beta_logical minus beta_aggression, which this OLS contract cannot test directly. The two categories can overlap in a comment, and a comment can be neither. Comments are unordered, with no timing or per-comment outcomes. Current text may contain outcome announcements, and the prompts exclude them. Associations only, not causal. The OC_comments list may be a subset of the discussion. The prompt returns share scalars per row, so semantic judgments rely on the annotator's interpretation of 'measured' and 'aggressive'. No scoring scale beyond the binary per-comment judgment is invented.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment (by another user) explicitly quotes or directly reproduces a specific factual claim from the OP's post AND, within that same comment, refutes it; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to identify what the OP claimed. Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (or closely reproduces verbatim) a specific factual claim made in the OP's title/argument, and (b) in that same comment argues that this factual claim is false, inaccurate or unsupported (refutation of the factual content, not merely of values, opinions or conclusions). Quotation and refutation must co-occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Quotes of other sources, or of non-factual/opinion statements, do not count. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome updates as evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output 0 or 1.

Acknowledgment must come before the divergence within the comment. Quoted OP text or mere restatement without affirming validity does not count; acknowledgment of unrelated minor points does not count. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy the conjunction. decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ concrete personal anecdotes are more likely associated with the original poster changing their view than those using abstract reasoning.

features.name: share_comments_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (OC_comments, other users) that use a concrete personal anecdote (commenter's own specific lived experience or event) as part of their argument.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own assertion includes a concrete personal anecdote: a specific first-person experience, event or situation from the commenter's (or their stated close acquaintance's) life used to argue against the OP. Do not count purely hypothetical examples, generic general-knowledge examples, or quoted/attributed text from others unless the commenter adopts it as their own experience. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change or delta-award announcement, post-outcome resolution update, or report of the outcome; such text is not evidence. Output = (comments with a personal anecdote) / (total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed input -> null.

features.name: share_comments_abstract_reasoning
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (OC_comments, other users) that argue through abstract reasoning (general principles, logic, definitions, generalized claims) rather than a concrete personal anecdote.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own argument relies on abstract reasoning: general principles, logical inference, definitions, general or statistical claims, or hypothetical/generic examples, without relying on a concrete personal anecdote. Comments that contain a concrete first-person anecdote as their argument do not count (overlap is not allowed for this feature); comments with neither (e.g. pure questions, jokes) do not count. Quotations of others count only if the commenter adopts them. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change or delta-award announcement, post-outcome resolution update, or report of the outcome. Output = (abstract-reasoning comments) / (total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed input -> null.

OC_comments and its text may contain delta announcements or outcome reports; semantic specs exclude them, but residual contamination risk remains. Comment-level lists may be incomplete, and the comparison is associational only. Comments of neither type exist, so the two shares need not sum to 1.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing at least three distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view than those with fewer.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument employs modest or uncertain epistemic markers are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using high-modality assertions.

Count only the OP's own assertions; ignore markers inside quotations from others unless the OP adopts them. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates and reports of the outcome. Return hedged_count / (hedged_count + high_modality_count) as a number in [0,1]. features.name: op_hedged_epistemic_marker_dominant
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument has more modest/uncertain epistemic markers than high-modality markers, 0 if more high-modality than modest; null if tied or none.
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's body). Count the OP's own modest/uncertain epistemic markers (e.g., 'maybe', 'I think', 'perhaps', 'might', 'seems', 'not sure') and own high-modality/certain markers (e.g., 'definitely', 'clearly', 'must', 'obviously', 'certainly', 'always'). Exclude quotations of others unless adopted, and exclude view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome updates and outcome reports. Return 1 if modest/uncertain count > high-modality count, 0 if high-modality count > modest count, null if equal (including both zero) or the argument is empty/missing.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between op_hedged_epistemic_marker_share and the likelihood of view change.

decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: modality markers are judged by the LLM with no fixed lexicon; the continuous hedged share is the primary measure and the binary dominance feature is an alternative coding of the same comparison (modest vs high-modality). Rows with no markers get null, so the test uses rows with at least one marker. Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements; these are excluded semantically but timing is unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments utilize a redrafting strategy, rewriting the original poster's viewpoint from a nuanced perspective before refutation, are associated with higher view change.

features.name: any_comment_redrafts_op_view_nuanced

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's argument contains explicit uncertainty markers are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_argument_has_uncertainty_marker

Exclude any OP view-change announcements, delta awards, edits reporting the outcome or post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: my view has changed', '∆'); these are not evidence. decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's initial argument explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument or limitation are directionally associated with a higher probability of view change.

Vague generic hypotheticals, unnamed examples, and quoted material not adopted by the commenter do not count. Ignore any text announcing that OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution/reports of outcome; these are not evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. For each comment decide whether it is a rebuttal of OP's view that proceeds by abstract logical reasoning, principles, definitions or generic hypotheticals and contains NO named real-world analogy/example (specific historical, scientific or otherwise named case) in the commenter's own assertions. Comments that contain a named real-world analogy, and non-rebuttal comments (questions, jokes, pure agreement), do not count. Return 1 if the title itself explicitly contains (a) an emotion word/expression of feeling (e.g., 'I hate', 'I'm afraid', 'love', 'angry', 'disgusted') or (b) a personal identifier: first-person self-reference or self-description (I, me, my, 'as a [identity/role]', personal experience). decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing multi-turn reply interactions in the conversation text are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: has_multi_turn_alternation

The conversation may include the OP's turns and later replies, and may contain view-change/delta announcements; this raw-text mechanical feature is not filtered for those, so outcome contamination is possible (the OP replying may itself follow persuasion). features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment by another user presents specific empirical evidence (concrete data, statistics, studies, documented cases/facts, cited sources) against the OP's view; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what each comment is countering. Return 1 if at least one comment itself asserts or cites specific empirical evidence (concrete statistics, data, named studies, documented historical/real-world cases, verifiable factual sources) as a counter to the OP's view; return 0 if no comment does. Evidence quoted from others counts only if the commenter cites it as support; quotation marks alone do not make it so. Vague appeals to common sense, anecdotes without specifics, and purely logical/conceptual arguments do not count. Ignore any text announcing OP view change, delta awards, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome; generic delta-rule discussion is neutral and not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Output only 0 or 1.

features.name: logical_refutation_only_discussion
features.definition: 1 if counter-argument comments include at least one purely logical refutation and none contains specific empirical evidence; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret the comments' targets. Return 1 if at least one comment offers a logical refutation (reasoning, consistency, definitional or conceptual argument against the OP's view) AND no comment in the list presents specific empirical evidence (concrete statistics, data, named studies, documented cases, cited factual sources). Return 0 otherwise (including when any comment has specific empirical evidence, or when no comment contains a logical refutation). Ignore text announcing OP view change, delta awards, post-outcome updates or outcome reports; generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. Quotations count only if adopted by the commenter. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Output only 0 or 1.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with specific empirical evidence in counter-arguments have the same association with delta as discussions with only logical refutations (coefficient on any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence is 0).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with specific empirical evidence in counter-arguments are more likely to have delta=1 than discussions with only logical refutations (coefficient on any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence is greater than that of logical_refutation_only_discussion).
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured. The listed term is evidence versus the omitted baseline (discussions with neither evidence nor logical-only refutation), not directly evidence versus logical-only; the exact contrast beta_evidence - beta_logical cannot be expressed as a single coefficient here. Operational assumptions: 'specific empirical evidence' = concrete data, studies, documented cases or sources; 'only logical refutations' = at least one logical refutation and no empirical-evidence comment. Comment lists are unordered with no timing; conversation was not used. Current text may include outcome announcements or later edits; prompts exclude them, but contamination risk remains. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the original argument before presenting a counter-example are associated with higher view change rates.

features.name: acknowledge_then_counterexample_comment
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment by another user explicitly acknowledges the validity of a specific component of the OP's argument and, in that same comment, then presents a counter-example; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what component of the OP's view a comment targets. Return 1 if at least one single comment (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific component/claim/point of the OP's argument is valid, correct or fair (a generic 'good point' with no specific component does not count), AND (b) then, in the same comment, presents a counter-example (a concrete case or instance that challenges the OP's view). Both conditions must occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Comment order is not chronology. Count only the commenter's own assertions, not text they merely quote from others unless adopted. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with acknowledge_then_counterexample_comment=1 have the same view-change rate as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with acknowledge_then_counterexample_comment=1 have a higher view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as "any comment" containing within-comment acknowledgment of a specific OP component followed by a counter-example; "before" is judged by order within the comment. Association only. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability). OC_comments may contain outcome-related text; the prompt excludes it, but residual contamination risk remains. Comment timing unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments utilize second-person direct address are associated with higher original poster view-change rates than arguments relying on third-person analysis.

features.name: share_comments_second_person_address
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (by other users) that use second-person direct address to the OP (e.g., addressing the OP as 'you/your' about their view, claims or situation).
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret who/what a comment targets. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own text directly addresses the OP in the second person (you/your/you're referring to the OP or their view, reasoning or experience). Generic 'you' meaning 'one/anyone', and 'you' inside quoted text attributed to others (including quoted OP text) do not count unless the commenter adopts it as direct address to the OP. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output the number of comments meeting the criterion divided by the total number of comments, as a float in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null.

features.name: share_comments_third_person_analysis
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (by other users) that rely on third-person analysis of the issue (discussing the topic, people or groups in the third person) without direct second-person address to the OP.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. For each comment, decide whether its argument is primarily third-person analysis of the topic, groups, evidence or situations (he/she/they/it/people/one, impersonal statements) AND the commenter does not directly address the OP as 'you/your' (generic 'you' meaning 'anyone' is not direct address). Comments with direct second-person address to the OP do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output the number of qualifying comments divided by the total number of comments, as a float in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: Holding share_comments_third_person_analysis fixed, share_comments_second_person_address has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Holding share_comments_third_person_analysis fixed, higher share_comments_second_person_address is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. Both named comparison groups are measured; the OLS coefficient on the second-person share is conditional on the third-person share and is not a direct contrast of the two (beta_A is not beta_A - beta_B). The shares can overlap or leave comments in neither group, since a comment can be neither addressed to the OP nor analytic. Comments are unordered, with no timestamps. Comments may be incomplete and conversation is not used. Text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompts are told to ignore. The 'primarily third-person analysis' judgment is an operational assumption. Discussion-level, not per-comment, outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Original posts with direct personal anecdotes in the argument are associated with a lower probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument body contains a direct personal anecdote (a specific experience the OP themself says happened to them or that they directly witnessed); else 0.
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, recounts at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific event or experience that happened to the OP or that the OP directly participated in or witnessed (e.g., 'when I was in college, my roommate...'). Return 0 if the argument has only general claims, hypotheticals, opinions, statistics, or third-party/quoted sources' experiences not adopted as the OP's own, or experiences of others merely reported. Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker. Do not count OP edits/announcements that they changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates as anecdote evidence. Generic mention of attitudes without a described experience is 0. Empty argument gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Output a single 0/1.

decomposed.h0: Original posts with a direct personal anecdote in the argument (op_argument_has_personal_anecdote=1) have the same probability of OP view change as those without.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_argument_has_personal_anecdote=1 have a lower probability of OP view change than those without.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements; these are excluded by the prompt but timing of text relative to outcome is unknown. 'Direct' is operationalized as the OP's own first-person experience or direct witnessing. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly introduce verifiable external facts distinct from the original argument are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_counter_external_fact
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment explicitly introduces a verifiable external fact (checkable statistic, study, event, law, documented source) not already present in the OP's title/argument; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion (or a cited source adopted as support), explicitly introduces a verifiable external fact (e.g., specific statistic, study, historical event, law, documented source or link) that is not already stated in the OP's title or argument; return 0 if none do. Opinions, reasoning, hypotheticals, and personal unverifiable anecdotes do not count. Background quotations of the OP or rebuttal-only quotes not adopted as support do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_counter_external_fact has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_counter_external_fact=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "verifiable external facts distinct from the original argument" is measured as any comment introducing such a fact (presence, not count). Verifiability is judged from text only, with no fact-checking. OC_comments may contain later or outcome-related text with unknown timing; the prompt excludes outcome announcements. Associational only, OLS on binary outcome (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument explicitly acknowledges the existence of alternative perspectives are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those presenting the argument as singularly deterministic.

features.name: op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument text explicitly acknowledges that alternative perspectives/views to their own exist; 0 otherwise.
features.spec: Read only the OP's `argument` text. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges the existence of alternative perspectives, opposing views, or other reasonable positions on the issue (e.g., 'some people think...', 'I know others disagree', 'there are other ways to see this'). Return 0 if no such acknowledgement is made, including when the argument is presented as the only possible conclusion. Do not count quotations attributed to others unless the OP adopts them as acknowledgement. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Empty or missing argument: null. Output a single 0/1.

features.name: op_argument_singularly_deterministic
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument is presented as singularly deterministic (only one possible conclusion, no alternatives acknowledged); 0 otherwise.
features.spec: Read only the OP's `argument` text. Return 1 if the OP presents their view as the single necessary or only possible conclusion, with no explicit acknowledgement of alternative perspectives (absolute, closed framing such as 'there is no other way to see this', 'objectively', 'must be'). Return 0 otherwise, including whenever alternatives are explicitly acknowledged. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and outcome reports. Empty or missing argument: null. Output a single 0/1.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives and the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change than other discussions.
decomposed.note: The comparison group is operationalized via the acknowledgement feature; the deterministic feature is defined for the contrast but omitted from rhs because it is nearly the complement (including both would risk collinearity). Non-acknowledging arguments that are not strongly deterministic fall in the reference group. Text is current argument text, which may contain edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); the prompt excludes these. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing multiple distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those containing only a single comment.

features.name: has_multiple_oc_comments
features.definition: 1 if the parsed OC_comments list has two or more entries, 0 if exactly one entry (single-comment discussion).
features.spec: import json; l=json.loads(x) for OC_comments; return null if missing/malformed/not a list; n=len(l); return 1 if n>=2, 0 if n==1; empty list (n==0) -> null since neither group applies. Equivalent: df['OC_comments'].map(lambda s: None if len(json.loads(s))==0 else int(len(json.loads(s))>=2)).

decomposed.h0: has_multiple_oc_comments has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_multiple_oc_comments=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with a single comment.
decomposed.note: Assumption: list entries are counted as comments; distinct commenters are not identifiable (the list may include multiple comments from one user), so 'distinct' is operationalized as separate list entries. Comments are by non-OP users. The list is the available set and may be truncated or filtered; it may include comments from after the outcome. Linear OLS on a binary outcome gives a linear probability model. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently embedding direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those lacking explicit textual anchoring.

features.name: share_comments_quoting_op
features.definition: Share of OC_comments counter-argument comments that directly quote wording from the OP's title or argument (explicit textual anchoring), by the commenter's own use of the quote.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). For each comment decide whether it contains a direct quotation (verbatim or near-verbatim excerpt, e.g. in quotation marks or markdown blockquote '>') of text from the OP's title or argument, used to anchor the reply. Use title and argument only to verify that quoted text comes from the OP. Quotes from other sources, or paraphrase without quoted wording, do not count. Ignore any content that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement or post-outcome resolution report; such content is not evidence. Output = (comments with OP quotation)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_quoting_op has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_quoting_op is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.note: "Frequently embedding" is operationalized as the share of comments in the row that quote the OP; no frequency threshold is invented. The comparison group (lacking anchoring) is represented by the low end of the share. Quotation detection is semantic: it must come from the commenter and be the OP's text, and the OP text is the current version, which may include edits. Comment order and timing are unknown. Rows with empty OC_comments get null. Associations only, not causal. OC_comments may contain delta announcements, which the prompt excludes.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments with specific real-world examples are associated with a higher probability of original poster view change than those lacking such citations.

features.name: any_counterarg_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment by another user, in its own assertions, cites a specific real-world example (named/concrete actual event, case, person, institution, study or documented instance) to support its counter-argument; else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers a specific real-world example (a concrete, identifiable actual event, case, person, organization, place, study or documented instance, including a concrete personal experience stated as actual) as support for its counter-argument. Return 0 if no comment does: only abstract reasoning, generic claims, hypotheticals or invented scenarios do not count. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it as support; quotations of the OP merely being rebutted do not count. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Output only 0 or 1.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_counterarg_specific_real_world_example equal to 1 have the same probability of OP view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_counterarg_specific_real_world_example equal to 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Assumes "containing counter-arguments with specific examples" means at least one comment. Association only (OLS linear probability). OC_comments may include text after the outcome and list order carries no chronology; the prompt excludes outcome announcements. "Specific" is judged by the LLM without a fixed scale.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments with higher lexical density are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_lexical_density
features.definition: Pooled lexical density of counter-argument comments: content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs by POS tag) divided by all word tokens across all OC_comments.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; if missing/malformed return null; if list empty or no word tokens return null. Concatenate all comment strings, tokenize into alphabetic word tokens (e.g. nltk word_tokenize, keep tokens with isalpha()), POS tag with nltk pos_tag (Penn tags). Content words = tokens tagged NN*, VB*, JJ*, RB* (excluding auxiliaries/modal MD). Value = content tokens / total alphabetic tokens (range 0-1). Not stopword-based.

decomposed.h0: oc_lexical_density has no association with the likelihood of OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_lexical_density is associated with a lower likelihood of delta=1.
decomposed.note: Lexical density operationalized as POS-based content-word share, pooled over all counter-comments (tokens pooled, so longer comments weigh more). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only. Comment text may contain quoted text or outcome/delta announcements; raw code does not filter these. Comment order/timing unknown; some comments may follow the view change.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that cite specific, localized examples are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_counter_specific_local_example
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment (by other users) cites a specific, localized example (a particular named/identifiable case, instance, event, or situation) as support, else 0.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, cites a specific, localized example (a particular identifiable case, event, person, place, instance, or concrete situation, not a generic or abstract category or hypothetical) in support of its counter-argument; return 0 if none does. Quoted material from the OP does not count; an example from an external source cited as support counts. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and any reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself an example. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

features.name: share_counter_comments_specific_local_example
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (other users) that cite a specific, localized example as support.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by non-OP users). Use title and argument only to interpret targets. Share = (number of comments that, in their own assertions, cite a specific, localized example: a particular identifiable case, event, person, place, instance or concrete situation, not generic or hypothetical) / (total number of comments). Do not count quoted OP text. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed gives null. Output a number in [0,1].

decomposed.h0: any_counter_specific_local_example has no association with the odds/probability of the OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_counter_specific_local_example = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. OLS on binary delta (linear probability model). Primary test is the 'any' feature; the share feature is a supplementary intensity measure not used in rhs. "Specific, localized example" is operationalized as a particular identifiable case/instance; no scale is supplied. Comments are unordered and have no timestamps; the current comment text may include or follow outcome-related content, and the semantic exclusions only reduce, not eliminate, that risk.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit hedging or self-doubt markers are associated with higher poster view-change rates than arguments presented with unwavering certainty.

features.name: argument_has_hedging_or_self_doubt
features.definition: 1 if the OP's own argument text contains at least one explicit hedging or self-doubt marker in the OP's own voice, else 0.
features.spec: Read only the argument text. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, uses at least one explicit hedging or self-doubt marker (e.g. 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'to my knowledge', 'I think' used as epistemic softening, 'it seems', 'possibly', admitting uncertainty about their own view). Return 0 if none. Ignore hedges inside quotations of other people unless the OP adopts them. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, and post-outcome resolution updates (e.g. 'EDIT: my view was changed', '!delta'); do not count them as evidence. Empty or missing argument gives null.

features.name: argument_unwavering_certainty
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument is presented with unwavering certainty: confident assertions and no explicit hedging or self-doubt markers in the OP's own voice.
features.spec: Read only the argument text. Return 1 if the OP presents their view with unwavering certainty: assertive, categorical claims and no explicit hedging or self-doubt markers (such as 'maybe', 'I might be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'perhaps', 'to my knowledge') in the OP's own voice. Return 0 if any such hedge or self-doubt appears, or if the argument is not presented with confident certainty (e.g. neutral/tentative). Hedges inside quotations of others are not the OP's own unless adopted. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, outcome-reporting edits and post-outcome updates. Empty or missing argument gives null.

decomposed.h0: Among discussions, argument_has_hedging_or_self_doubt is not associated with delta rates, holding argument_unwavering_certainty fixed.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_has_hedging_or_self_doubt=1 have higher view-change rates than those with argument_unwavering_certainty=1.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured. Because unwavering certainty is by construction nearly the complement of hedging (hedged arguments are always 0 on certainty), the two are close to collinear; the baseline is arguments that are neither hedged nor confidently certain, so the hedging coefficient is not exactly hedged-vs-certain contrast (that would be beta_hedge - beta_certain). Hedging is judged on current argument text, which may include edits/outcome announcements (excluded semantically); timing relative to outcome is unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain concrete, locally verifiable examples are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract principles.

features.name: share_comments_concrete_verifiable_examples
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (by other users) that contain at least one concrete, locally verifiable example (specific case, named instance, checkable fact or data point) offered in the commenter's own voice or adopted as support.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than OP. Use title and argument only to interpret what each comment targets. For each comment decide whether it contains at least one concrete, locally verifiable example: a specific case, named instance, particular event, or specific checkable fact/figure/source that supports its counter-argument. Quotations count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Purely general principles, hypotheticals without specifics, or vague appeals do not count. Ignore any text that announces OP view change, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution; do not treat these as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. Output the number of qualifying comments divided by total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null. The list order carries no meaning.

features.name: share_comments_abstract_principles
features.definition: Share of counter-argument comments (by other users) that rely mainly on abstract principles or general reasoning, with no concrete, locally verifiable example.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than OP. Use title and argument only to interpret each comment's target. For each comment decide whether it relies on abstract principles (general rules, theoretical or moral claims, generalized reasoning) AND contains no concrete, locally verifiable example (no specific case, named instance, or checkable fact/figure). Comments with such an example are not counted. Ignore OP view-change/delta announcements and post-outcome resolution text as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. Output qualifying comments divided by total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null. List order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_concrete_verifiable_examples has no association with the probability of OP view change, holding share_comments_abstract_principles constant.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_concrete_verifiable_examples is associated with a higher probability of OP view change, holding share_comments_abstract_principles constant.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis is at discussion level, operationalized as the share of comments of each type; "locally verifiable" is interpreted as specific, checkable instances/facts. Neither-type comments are possible. The single coefficient does not express the contrast concrete minus abstract; both named sides are measured. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only. Current comment text may contain outcome announcements or later replies; prompts exclude them but timing is unknown and no comment timestamps exist.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain concrete real-world examples are associated with higher original-poster view change rates than those relying solely on abstract logic.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_example
features.definition: 1 if at least one counter-argument comment by another user offers its own concrete real-world example (specific real event, case, person, data instance, or personal/real-life instance) as support; 0 if comments are present but rely only on abstract reasoning.
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Return 1 if at least one comment itself asserts a concrete real-world example (specific named or described real event, case, person, organization, statistic tied to a real instance, or real-life experience) to support its counter-argument. Return 0 if the list is non-empty and no comment does so (comments rely solely on abstract logic, hypotheticals, or general principles). Purely hypothetical/invented scenarios do not count. Examples that appear only inside quotations of the OP or others count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null. Output a single 0/1 value.}

decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_example=1 have a higher OP view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "contain concrete examples" is measured as any comment with one; "solely abstract logic" is the 0 group (non-empty comments with none). Mixed discussions fall in group 1. Rows with empty comment lists get 0 per policy, though they are neither group. Comments are unordered and the current text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. Association only, not causal. OLS on a binary outcome gives a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit conditional language linking outcomes to specific antecedent conditions are associated with a lower likelihood of view change.

features.name: argument_has_explicit_conditional_outcome_language
features.definition: 1 if the OP's argument body (not title, comments) contains explicit conditional language in the OP's own voice linking an outcome/consequence to a specific antecedent condition (e.g., 'if X, then Y', 'unless', 'provided that'); else 0.
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions (not merely in quotations attributed to others unless adopted), uses explicit conditional language that links an outcome or consequence to a specific antecedent condition, such as 'if X then Y', 'if X, Y would happen', 'unless X, Y', 'provided that', 'as long as', 'when X, Y follows' with a clear condition and outcome. Return 0 if there is no such construction (vague hedges, rhetorical 'if you ask me', or conditions without a stated outcome do not count). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes, or post-outcome resolution updates as evidence; conditionals appearing only there do not count. Empty text gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Output 0/1.

For each comment, decide whether its rebuttal rests on abstract, theoretical, or general principle-based reasoning (conceptual argument, logic, definitions, general mechanisms) and contains no concrete personal anecdote. Comments with a personal anecdote, or that are not rebuttals, do not count. Quoted material not adopted by the commenter is not the commenter's reasoning.
